title: Finite coproducts and evaluation on finite disjoint unions
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let X_proetale be its pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let I be a finite set and, for each i in I, let V_i be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated object of X_proetale [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. The scheme disjoint union V=\coprod_{i\in I}V_i exists in the qcqs subsite and is affine when every V_i is affine. Writing h_W=Hom_X(-,W) for the representable presheaf, the canonical morphism of sheaves of sets [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with the coproduct taken in that category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], \coprod_{i\in I}h_{V_i}\to h_V is an isomorphism, and for every sheaf of sets F on X_proetale the induced map F(V)\to\prod_{i\in I}F(V_i) is a natural bijection, including the empty family I=\varnothing, where V=\varnothing and F(∅) is a singleton.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] to construct $V=\coprod_i V_i$, the morphism $V\to X$, and the pairwise disjoint clopen coprojections $\iota_i$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct-lfp-qcqs] makes $V$ qcqs. If $V_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ for all $i$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum] identifies $V$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_i A_i)$. For the empty index set this is the spectrum of the zero ring, namely the empty scheme.

The structural map $V\to X$ is weakly etale: at $v\in V_i$ its stalk map is the stalk map of $V_i\to X$, so it is flat; near $\Delta(v)$ the open subscheme $V_i\times_X V_i$ of $V\times_X V$ identifies the diagonal stalk map with that of $V_i\to X$, so the diagonal is flat as well. This checks the two defining conditions of [def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism] using [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Likewise each clopen inclusion $V_i\to V$ has identity stalk maps and diagonal an isomorphism, hence is weakly etale. The empty scheme has no points, so both flatness conditions are vacuous. Finite unions of bounded schemes remain in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention]; after taking the chosen skeleton, $V$ is therefore an object of the qcqs full subcategory of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

The family $\{V_i\to V\}$ covers in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]: for an affine open $A\subset V$, each $A\cap V_i$ is clopen in $A$, hence quasi-compact; take a finite affine open cover of each $A\cap V_i$ and combine these finitely many covers. Their images cover $A$, which verifies the stated covering criterion. The empty family covers the empty scheme by the same criterion. The equalizer sheaf axiom in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] applied to that empty cover gives $F(\varnothing)$ a single element. For the cover of $V$, the overlaps $V_i\times_V V_j$ are empty for $i\ne j$ and $V_i$ for $i=j$. Off-diagonal compatibility is automatic because $F(\varnothing)$ is a singleton; on-diagonal both maps are the identity. Thus every tuple in $\prod_i F(V_i)$ glues uniquely to a section of $F(V)$, proving the asserted bijection. For a morphism $\eta:F\to G$, naturality gives $G(\iota_i)\eta_V=\eta_{V_i}F(\iota_i)$ for each $i$, proving naturality of the bijection.

By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-subcanonical], $h_V$ and each $h_{V_i}$ are sheaves. Since sheaves form a full subcategory of presheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection] identifies restriction along $h_{\iota_i}$ with $F(\iota_i)$ under $\operatorname{Hom}(h_W,F)\cong F(W)$. Step 3 therefore gives, for every sheaf $F$, the bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(h_V,F)\cong\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(h_{V_i},F)$ induced by the coprojections. This is precisely the coproduct universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Hence $h_V$, with these coprojections, is their coproduct in sheaves; the canonical morphism from any chosen coproduct has inverse supplied by its universal property, and both composites are identities because their restrictions to all coprojections are identities. This also proves the empty-family assertion: $h_{\varnothing}$ is initial in sheaves.
